title: Trimming on a cycle with a crew limit

blocks.text: A municipal utility (a fictional one) trims the trees along each of its circuits on a fixed cycle: a circuit is **due** in year $`y`$ when at least `cycle` years have passed since it was last trimmed ($`y - \text{last} \ge \text{cycle}`$). Its crews can trim at most `capacity` miles a year, and a circuit is trimmed whole or not at all. Work that is due and not done stays due.
Write `plan_trims(circuits, cycle, capacity, years)` in `trims.py`. `circuits` maps a circuit id to `(miles, year last trimmed)`. For each year of `years`, in order, the crews:

items: take the circuits that are due, the one trimmed longest ago first (ties by circuit id);
trim each one whose miles fit in what is left of the year's capacity, and pass over any that do not, going on down the list;
record a trimmed circuit's new last-trim year, so its cycle restarts.

blocks.text: The result maps each year to a pair: the ids trimmed that year, sorted, and the **backlog**, the miles that were due that year but not trimmed. The backlog counts every circuit due and left untrimmed, whenever it first fell due: a circuit carried over from an earlier year counts again in each year it is still waiting, and a circuit longer than `capacity`, which no year can trim, counts in every year from the one it falls due.

Before you code, trace the instance with A (50 miles, last 2018), B (10, 2019), C (10, 2020), a 3-year cycle and 25 miles of capacity through 2024 by hand. The tests use small instances like it. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from trims import plan_trims

circuits = {"North": (40, 2026), "East": (25, 2027), "South": (35, 2027), "West": (15, 2028)}

plan = plan_trims(circuits, 4, 50, [2030, 2031, 2032, 2033])
for year, (trimmed, backlog) in plan.items():
    print(f"{year} at 50 miles a year: trimmed {trimmed}, miles left due {backlog}")

cases.says: with room for everything, each circuit is trimmed when due and again a cycle later
miles due but not trimmed are the year's backlog and come back the next year
the circuit longest since its last trim is trimmed first
a circuit too long for what is left does not stop shorter ones behind it
a circuit longer than any year's capacity is carried over and counts in the backlog every year
